cards.text: The Roman commander just learned that Paul, the apostle he put in chains, is a Roman citizen (Acts 22:29). The next day, wanting to learn the real reason Paul is accused by the Jews, he orders the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin, the Jewish ruling council, to assemble. That's not a meeting, friend, that's the WHOLE group chat showing up in person.

cards.question: The commander keeps Paul in chains when he brings him before the Sanhedrin.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The commander releases Paul, brings him down and has him stand before them. Paul looks directly at the Sanhedrin, and there's no small talk and no warm-up.

cards.question: Paul opens by telling the Sanhedrin how he has lived before God. What does he claim?

answers.text: His conscience has been good to this day
He has broken the law many times
He has lived in fear of the council

cards.text: Paul gets one sentence out. Then Ananias (not the Ananias who restored Paul's sight in Acts 22:13) orders the men standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

cards.question: Ananias, who orders Paul struck on the mouth, is the ___.

answers.text: high priest
commander
centurion

cards.text: Paul fires right back: "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall!" Friend, I've been called crumbly, dusty and blurry, but never a WHITEWASHED WALL.

cards.question: Paul says the man who gave the order sits there to judge him by the law. How does Paul say that man breaks the law himself?

answers.text: By ordering that Paul be struck
By judging Paul on the Sabbath
By taking money from the crowd

cards.text: Those standing nearby say, "How dare you insult the high priest of God!" Uh-oh.

cards.question: Paul says he was not aware that the man he called a whitewashed wall was the high priest.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Paul calls them brothers and quotes Exodus 22:28. What does that Scripture say not to do?

answers.text: Speak evil about the ruler of your people
Bring your brother before the judges
Turn away from the elders of your people

cards.text: Paul knows some of the Sanhedrin are Sadducees and the others Pharisees, two groups of Jewish leaders. He calls out that he's a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee, on trial because of his hope in the resurrection of the dead.

cards.question: As soon as Paul says he's on trial because of his hope in the resurrection, what happens in the Sanhedrin?

answers.text: A dispute splits the Pharisees and Sadducees
The whole council calls for his death
The high priest ends the meeting at once

cards.text: The assembly is divided. That's what happens when somebody asks the break room who touched the thermostat.

cards.question: Why does Paul's line about the resurrection divide the Pharisees and the Sadducees?

answers.text: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection
The Pharisees say Paul has left the law
The Sadducees say Paul is no Pharisee

cards.question: The Pharisees acknowledge the resurrection, angels and spirits.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: A great clamor rises, and some scribes, teachers of the law from the party of the Pharisees, get up and argue sharply. The dead batteries I shared that drawer with used to fight over who had the most charge left, and even THEY never got this loud.

cards.question: The scribes from the party of the Pharisees demand that Paul be punished.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The scribes say, "We find nothing wrong with this man."

cards.question: The scribes from the party of the Pharisees go on with a question about Paul. What do they wonder might have happened?

answers.text: A spirit or an angel spoke to him
The Sadducees paid him to stir trouble
The commander sent him to test them

cards.question: The dispute grows so violent that the commander is afraid they will tear Paul to pieces. He orders soldiers to remove Paul by force and bring him into the ___.

answers.text: barracks
temple
palace

cards.text: The following night, the Lord stands near Paul and says, "Take courage!" After a day like that, I bet Paul needed to hear it.

cards.question: The Lord tells Paul that his testifying about Him is finished now that he has testified in Jerusalem.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The Lord says that as Paul has testified about Him in Jerusalem, he must testify in Rome too. We're setting this batch aside for now, friend, but Paul's story is a long way from over.
